ns2:section.sectionText: Topic: The Literature of Immigration This class is devoted to studying the literature of US immigration, with a special emphasis on twenty-first-century writing. We will be doing several kinds of reading, including memoirs, short fiction, novels, and historical documents. That broad base of preparation will enable us to pursue several key themes: assimilation, affiliation, and alienation. We will also see how these writings also explore prevailing national anxieties, such as racial inequality, class identity, and gender status. At the same time, we will also be considering how immigrants have been greeted in the US and the kinds of concerns to which immigration—legal and illegal—give rise. In these ways, students will become familiar with the discourse of immigration: what we, as people and as a people, mean when we talk about immigration. Students will be able to explore the interests they develop in a series of short papers and in a variety of assignments that are designed to help students write more effectively at the majors’ level.
